Skeuomorph Mobile Banking

The Dribbble concept that started the trend: a banking app molded out of one pale blue-gray surface.

Source
Dribbble (archived copy)
Creator
Alexander (Oleksandr) Plyuto, for Heartbeat Agency
Made
2019 (posted 5 November 2019, per the Wayback copy of the shot page)
Style
Neumorphism (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Soft, tactile, calm
Evidence
Opened the shot’s main image (frame_8_4x.png, 1600 × 1200) from cdn.dribbble.com, found through the Wayback capture of 15 November 2019. The live Dribbble page returned an empty body to scripts. Only the first image of the shot was inspected; the other images in the shot were not.
Reviewed
28 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

The description reads: “Let’s imagine that we live in a dimension where skeuomorph is still alive and continued its evolution in mobile interfaces. What would applications look like then? Here is my vision.” A later update links a Figma file, “Skeuomorph Style Guide”.

The Wayback capture of 15 November 2019 shows 129,538 views and 2,644 likes. Malewicz wrote in December 2019 that the shot “gained over 3000 likes and pushed the trend forward”.

In 2019 Dribbble credited the shot to “Alexander Plyuto for Heartbeat Agency”; search results in 2026 show the name “Oleksandr Plyuto”.

Observed

  • Two phone-sized panels and a settings card on a pale blue-gray background. The panels, cards, and buttons have the same color as the background.
  • Each raised shape has a white highlight on its upper left and a soft blue-gray shadow on its lower right. The credit-limit bar, the active tab in the bottom bar, and the back/menu button pair look pressed in.
  • A large round chart is carved into the surface with ridges between segments. One segment is a raised orange wedge with a gradient; a small red button sits in its center.
  • Two accents break the monochrome: a glossy red rocker switch with ridges (“OFF”) and an iridescent patch on the credit card.
  • Type is a geometric sans-serif in dark navy, bold for “Statistic” and “Balance”, regular for labels. The card number uses a monospaced face.

Why it belongs

This is neumorphism before its name. The surface recipe is already complete, but the red rocker switch, the chip, and the iridescent foil keep objects from skeuomorphism. Later work dropped them and kept only the pale surface and the paired shadows.

Borrow

Carve a chart into the surface as a pressed dial and raise only the selected segment, so that selection reads as height.
